quote:
To ensure further
successional development, remnant forest should be in
proximity so that there would be sufﬁcient input of seeds.

relationship.requirement: Remnant forest should be in proximity to supply seeds for further succession.
relationship.note: Proximity requirement supports nearer forest, but source gives no distance cutoff, response scores or calibrated curve.

context.region: Degraded tropical forestlands; review informed particularly by Asian practice
context.practice_as_described: Assisted natural regeneration (ANR): release existing woody regeneration, suppress weeds and prevent disturbance. No experimental comparator; guidance for site selection.
context.note: Printed page 621, Rationale for Using ANR and Required Conditions. Distance is the inverse of proximity; decreasing denotes closer remnant forest, not a quantified dose-response. Requirement concerns continued succession, not proof that distant sites cannot establish. Enrichment planting is an alternative if propagules are insufficient. VONT distance_to_forest remains pending_review; no dataset binding or analytical cutoff is created.

selection_justification:
ANR is most suitable for restoring areas where some level
of natural succession is in progress.

raw_name: lack of awareness and demonstrative results
quote:
Despite its practical advantages, ANR remains underutil-
ized due to lack of awareness and demonstrative results.

relationship.factor: Lack of awareness and demonstration of results
relationship.constraint: Authors attribute underuse of assisted natural regeneration to this knowledge and demonstration gap.
relationship.note: Review judgement, not a measured adoption effect, national governance score or proof of a financial barrier.

context.region: Degraded tropical forestlands; review informed particularly by Asian practice
context.practice_as_described: Assisted natural regeneration (ANR) restores degraded forestlands through protection and release of natural woody regeneration. No treatment-control comparison for this adoption assertion.
context.note: Printed page 624, Discussion. Source explicitly requests systematic application, monitoring and validation of personal experience. Operational enabling evidence for extension and demonstration, not T4 suitability or an effect of restoration on governance.

quote:
Long-term community involve-
ment and support is critical in preventing the reoccurrence
of disturbance events that will set back succession to the
before-treatment state.

relationship.constraint: Community involvement supports prevention of recurrent disturbance that reverses assisted regeneration.
relationship.note: Author guidance about participatory protection, not a quantified governance effect or geographic suitability gate.

context.region: Degraded tropical forestlands; review informed particularly by Asian practice
context.practice_as_described: Assisted natural regeneration (ANR) restores degraded forestlands through protection and release of natural woody regeneration. No treatment-control comparison for this adoption assertion.
context.note: Printed page623, Protection From Disturbance. Participatory governance supports continued site protection from fire, grazing and human disturbance. Distinct from awareness-limited adoption on page624; not an independent source vote. No quantified effectiveness, fire hazard threshold or exclusion inferred.
